Before adoption the 2.1.316 list still applies, plus exact-host strict validation of the packaged plugin, installer behaviour when `claude mcp add` waits or exits 1, the fast-exit handshake pin and `deniedMcpServers` matching. No managed, cloud, gateway or sandbox assurance, binary upgrade or active writer restart follows from this note review. 2026-11-14 review: release notes 2.1.285 to 2.1.325 read for the surfaces the plugin uses (plugin load and commands, the skills-dir plugin, plugin.json, hooks.json, .mcp.json, the PreToolUse hook and its exit-code contract, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR); the installer reads only the strict validator's exit code. Admit 2.1.311, the stable release published 2026-10-26 and older than the 14-day floor, for the plugin's exercised profile only: exact-host strict validator, isolated plugin load, install/upgrade/removal, unverified-version refusal, and an MCP hub live claim with allowed and denied writes. 2.1.284 is the rollback version. Cancellation/resume and transcript handling stay unqualified: they need an authenticated model turn, which needs the owner's word; the plugin uses neither. No credential operation, managed, cloud or sandbox assurance follows; 2.1.312 and later stay unqualified. 2026-11-14 reading: official notes 2.1.323 (published 2026-11-12) and 2.1.325 (published 2026-11-13) were read in full from the release API the watch uses. The stored digest is the 2.1.325 body and already matches, so the hash stays. 2.1.325 fixes decoding of zstd-compressed responses. For this package's plugin profile the two notes change hook, MCP and permission behaviour that 2.1.311 is not claimed to have. plugin.json engines["claude-code"] refuses install, update and load outside the stated range, and install picks the newest release that fits. claude plugin validate type-checks a plugin's TypeScript hooks (a finding is a warning unless --strict, which the packaged installer already requires as an exit code) and checks the $ nouns a mod's engine.create hook adds. A 30-second hook heartbeat runs in claude -p and SDK sessions. Plugin commands and claude mcp list could sign a Console profile out when they ended during token renewal. A WorktreeCreate hook from a plugin in CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_SEED_DIR was skipped on the first run in a new home. /mcp kept listing a plugin MCP server removed by a reload while it was connecting. An MCP server stayed "needs authentication" and its mcp_tool hooks were skipped after a token refresh that was refused only for a moment. Headless MCP elicitation was cancelled without asking after a reconnect, and an SDK host answered "Not connected" after a tool call had reconnected the server. Deny and ask rules starting mcp__plugin_*_ missed a plugin server or tool spelled in another letter case. A removed and re-added MCP server stayed disconnected. A --plugin-dir hook hang printed nothing on text-output claude -p. A null tools-list entry ended a headless session. CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN re-ran a turn a hook's continue: false had stopped. HTTP hooks returned HTTP 500 on Linux when CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB was set and the sandbox was off. claude -p and the SDK ran Bash unsandboxed when sandbox settings failed validation, and now stop at start-up. Earlier MCP calls were missing on resume when the server connected late. Stop during UserPromptSubmit or a plugin prompt hook was shown as an error. Bash gaps in the same notes are acceptance items and not a sandbox qualification: lsof without a prompt, rm judged from the wrong folder, an attached-wildcard allow rule, combined sudo flags, sandbox.excludedCommands letting an unnamed command leave the sandbox, the sandbox switching off mid-session, compound commands running without asking, an allow rule running a different program than it names, sandboxed writes to the native updater download folder, and incomplete protection of a worktree's settings and hooks, a linked worktree's shared git folder, the legacy config and checkpoint copies. A committed .claude/settings.local.json could be treated as the user's own in some subfolders. The verified version stays 2.1.311 and 2.1.284 stays the rollback; 2.1.323 and 2.1.325 stay unqualified. Before adopting anything newer, add to the acceptance list the engines range against the packaged plugin, a fresh-home WorktreeCreate hook, MCP removal during connect, mcp_tool hooks after a refused refresh, mcp__plugin_*_ case folding, a hook continue: false that is not re-run, Bash compound-command permission and allow-rule program identity, and sandbox protection of worktree settings and hooks. No credential operation, managed, cloud or sandbox assurance, binary upgrade, or active writer restart.

Before any 1.x migration the 1.2.0 acceptance list still applies, plus exact-host extension load/resume, header hooks, denied writes, cancellation and usage attribution. No credentials, model calls or restart authorised. 2026-11-06 security review: 1.5.0 rejects non-http(s) MCP OAuth metadata URLs that a malicious server could hand to the platform URL handler, fixes amplified glob patterns (denial of service), control characters in sign-in URLs and terminal titles injecting escape sequences, a saved 'Do not trust' decision being ignored, pi.exec() never returning when a command ignores SIGTERM, and updates undici to 8.12.3. Tool argument validation moves to pi-schema; the packaged extension registers hooks and no tool schemas, so that break does not reach it. Retain exercised 0.87.1 RPC/claim extension and 0.86.0 rollback; 0.87.1 is not claimed to have these fixes, which makes the 1.x qualification the priority for this surface. A session whose original folder was moved or deleted can be forked into the current folder.
